17748478-21b7-4400-ae1f-363effe5688e@ufc.why: Ciryl Gane makes the first defense of his UFC heavyweight title against unbeaten #4 contender Josh Hokit, a fight that sets the tone for the division. In the co-main event, bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison defends her belt against former two-division champion Amanda Nunes, who is attempting a comeback after walking away from the sport in 2023.
17748478-21b7-4400-ae1f-363effe5688e@ufc.know: A numbered UFC event like this one is usually reserved for the promotion's biggest nights, often built around a title fight; this card has two. Harrison and Nunes were once training partners at the same gym, which adds a personal layer to their matchup, while Hokit, a former college wrestler, remains undefeated as a fast-rising heavyweight prospect.

b0ab8af8-cb28-465a-aea7-5d32bec5ae19@nin.why: The 49ers are 7-1 and sitting atop the NFC West, the strongest record in their division this year. Dallas is a middling 3-5 team, so this is a good chance for San Francisco to pad its division lead. No playoff spot is clinched or lost here, it is simply one more step toward a strong playoff seed.
b0ab8af8-cb28-465a-aea7-5d32bec5ae19@nin.know: It is only Week 10, so one game will not decide anyone's season. Instead watch how the 49ers handle a mediocre opponent on the road, and track injuries to running back Christian McCaffrey and receiver Deebo Samuel, both nursing hamstring issues, plus tight end George Kittle, a key target in the short passing game Dallas's coach has flagged as hard to stop.

fe74ebe2-bd22-454c-bd51-783a4e7a50cf@ufc.why: Former light heavyweight champ Jiri Prochazka looks to rebound after an April title-fight knockout loss, while unbeaten rising prospect Navajo Stirling, fresh off stopping ex-champ Jan Blachowicz, tries to prove he belongs among the elite. In the co-main, former bantamweight champ Aljamain Sterling, now up at featherweight, meets surging contender Kevin Vallejos, with the winner moving closer to a title shot at 145 pounds.
fe74ebe2-bd22-454c-bd51-783a4e7a50cf@ufc.know: UFC rankings run #1 to #15 in each weight class below the champion; beating a higher-ranked foe builds a case for a title shot, the chance to fight for the belt. A Fight Night card has no title bout but is a good place to spot fighters who may soon reach title contention.
